objective_for_doctor: A 11-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have right side of the chest pain, left side of the chest pain, and lightheadedness/near-fainting.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. I’m having chest pain on both sides—right and left, and it feels sharp and crampy, kind of in the right breast area too. I also feel really short of breath, lightheaded like I might faint, nauseous, and I had palpitations—plus I felt numb/tingly in both arms and legs and around my mouth, and like I was detached from my body or surroundings.
Doctor: I’m going to ask a few quick questions to make sure this is safe. When did the symptoms start, and is the chest pain worse with breathing, movement, or lying down?

It started pretty fast—like an onset speed of about 5 out of 10. The pain is around 4 out of 10, and it’s mainly on the chest but I don’t know for sure if it’s worse with breathing, movement, or lying down.

Doctor: I need to clarify: do you have any fever/cough, recent injury, recent long travel, or any personal/family history of heart disease, blood clots, or sudden death? Also, during the episode have you actually passed out, and is your heart rate unusually fast or irregular right now?

No fever or cough. No recent injury. No long travel. I don’t have a known personal history of heart disease or blood clots, and I don’t know about family heart disease or sudden death. I didn’t fully pass out—more like near-fainting. Right now I feel my heart is beating fast and sometimes irregular during the episode.

Doctor: I’m concerned about possible heart rhythm problems or less commonly a clot/other cause—right now, when was the last episode, and do you currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, or lightheadedness at rest (yes/no)?  
Doctor: Also, can you tell me your heart rate if you’ve checked it (or describe how fast), and did the numbness/tingling around your mouth and limbs happen during the palpitations?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: 12-lead_ECG.

The last episode was recently—this is happening now. Yes, I currently have chest pain, shortness of breath, and lightheadedness at rest. I haven’t measured my heart rate with a number, but it feels fast and sometimes off/irregular during the palpitations; the numbness/tingling around my mouth and in my arms and legs happened during the palpitations too.

Doctor: Given you’re having ongoing chest pain, shortness of breath, near-fainting, and palpitations with mouth/limb tingling, I’m worried about a potentially dangerous heart rhythm issue—**right now I want you to stay seated/lying down and I’m treating this as urgent**; do you have any visible swelling/pain in one leg or coughing up blood?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Repeat vital_signs_BP_oxygen_saturation.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Continuous_ECG/telemetry.
No visible swelling or pain in one leg. No coughing up blood. I’m staying seated/lying down as you asked.

Doctor: I’m going to quickly confirm one thing: any severe sweating, worsening chest pressure, or new weakness/confusion right now, and have you taken any stimulants/energy drinks, caffeine, decongestants, or asthma inhalers today?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Troponin_level, CBC, electrolytes_(BMP), and Thyroid_function_tests.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

I’m very anxious and I feel scared like I might die, but I don’t know about severe sweating—no one has told me I’m sweating a lot. My chest pain is still there and I feel short of breath and lightheaded, but I don’t think I have new weakness or confusion.  
I didn’t take energy drinks/caffeine/decongestants today, and I haven’t used an asthma inhaler today.

Doctor: I’m going to treat this as **urgent** given ongoing chest pain, shortness of breath, near-fainting, palpitations, and tingling around the mouth/hands—this pattern can be from an abnormal heart rhythm and needs immediate evaluation, so please call emergency services/activate a code now if not already. While we wait for the ECG/telemetry and labs (ECG, troponin, BMP/electrolytes, thyroid, chest X-ray), can you tell me your age/weight and whether you’ve ever had fainting or unexplained seizures during exercise or stress?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any known genetic heart condition in the family (e.g., long QT, cardiomyopathy) or sudden death before age 50?

I’m 11 years old. I don’t know my exact weight right now.  

I haven’t fainted fully or had unexplained seizures during exercise or stress—just near-fainting like I might pass out during these episodes. I don’t know of any genetic heart condition in the family or sudden death before age 50.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—this is still an emergency: while we’re getting results, stay seated/lying down and tell someone nearby to call/confirm EMS. Do you have any asthma history, anxiety/panic attacks, or have you taken any medications recently (including cough meds, stimulants like ADHD meds, or cold/flu products)?

Yes, I have asthma history—I’ve had to use a bronchodilator before, but I didn’t use it today. I do have anxiety and I’ve had panic-type feelings before, but I haven’t taken any medicines recently like cough meds, ADHD stimulants, or cold/flu products.

Doctor: Given your ongoing chest pain, shortness of breath, near-fainting, and palpitations with mouth/limb tingling—even with anxiety/asthma history—I’m treating this as a potentially dangerous heart rhythm problem until proven otherwise; have you been able to call EMS/rapid response, and can you keep someone with you in the room?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Venous_blood_gas_(or_arterial_gas_if_needed)_(for_hypoxia/acid-base) and Serum_mg_calcium_levels.  
Doctor: While those are running, are you currently having any wheezing or needing your rescue inhaler, or is breathing difficulty present even without wheeze?

I haven’t called EMS myself yet, but I can tell someone nearby right now to call/confirm. I’ll keep someone with me in the room.  

Right now I’m having breathing difficulty even without wheezing, and I’m not using my rescue inhaler.

Doctor: I need you to **call EMS right now** (or have the person with you call) for ongoing chest pain + shortness of breath + near-fainting with palpitations. I’m treating this as **urgent/possible life-threatening arrhythmia** while we get: ECG, continuous telemetry, vitals/oxygen, troponin, electrolytes/BMP, CBC, thyroid tests, chest X-ray, and venous blood gas + calcium.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: **Suspected acute cardiac arrhythmia causing presyncope (possible SVT/ventricular arrhythmia or channelopathy like long-QT); emergency evaluation required.**
